## Biography

A black hole. Not the largest in the galaxy — Sagittarius A* holds that title — but one of the most ominously named. The Great Annihilator sits below the galactic plane, its accretion disk a bruise of X-ray radiation against the dark.

The Children Of The Core survey operated near this singularity in 3309, the Fimbulthul assigned to support their search for Earth-like worlds toward the galactic core. The Azura Initiative established itself in the same region, proving that human communities can persist even in the shadow of something that devours light. Pilots who visit the Annihilator report a psychological effect: the sense that the sky above is wrong, that down and up have exchanged meanings, that the galaxy's familiar geography has been inverted.

The name is melodramatic. The physics are not.
